chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: Living in Harlem with the Spratley family
summary: Between Ernie Fields and Newark he lived on 118th Street with the Spratleys, kin to a drummer he knew.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you went to New York but actually you stopped off -- did you stop off with Ernie Fields, I mean you were with him for a short while, then you went to New York, or this was a little later?
No, this comes later. I did join Ernie because he played the Apollo Theater. When my job ran out in Newark, I moved back into Harlem.
Do you remember where you lived in Harlem?
In Harlem? Yes, on 118th Street between Lenox and --
118th between Lenox and I guess that would be 7th Avenue.

Yes. That's where I was, 118th Street with a family by the name of Spratley (phonetic spelling). Where I happened to know the Spratleys because her brother was the famous Hot Lips Hackett. He was a drummer, he used to play with Irving C. Miller's road shows and he told me if I ever get to
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

New York to look up his sister, so I did and they had an extra room in the back, that's where I stayed with the sister. I happened to hang around the Rhythm Club and I made my contacts there and I'd get a gig there once in a while and I ran into a fella now that's doing "One Mo' Time" by the name of Jabbo Smith, one of the trumpet greats.
